records.summary: Türkiye imposed electricity cuts on its organised industrial zones from 24 January 2022, announced by the transmission operator as three days, and restricted gas to large users after gas deliveries from Iran fell sharply.
records.effect: The transmission operator announced three days of power outages in organised industrial zones (24 to 26 January 2022); gas-fired power plants were ordered to cut gas use by 40% and distributors to cut supply to large consumers to 60%, heating excepted. Carmakers and other manufacturers suspended or reduced production.

records.summary: On 16 May 2022 a dust storm halted flights at three of Iraq's airports, closed schools nationwide and led authorities in seven of the country's 18 provinces to shut government offices. records.summary: A failure of Bangladesh's national grid on 4 October 2022 cut electricity to most of the country for about seven hours.
records.effect: The outage began at about 14:00 and power was fully restored at 21:00. The power development board said transmission failed in the east of the country and that the cause was under investigation, probably a technical malfunction. AFP reported at least 130 million people without power and more than 80 percent of the country affected. A garment manufacturers' association said factories could not run without power and offices had to close. Mobile services were disrupted because operators' backup power was insufficient, the telecom regulator said. The grid company's probe found negligence by two of its engineers, and the government decided to suspend them.

records.summary: During an early cold wave in late May 2024 Argentina's gas regulator declared a pre-emergency and gas supply was cut to industrial users and to CNG filling stations to keep households and businesses supplied.
